prompt: Here's a rate limiter we run in front of a production API — a NestJS guard that throttles requests per-IP (or per-user) using Redis to track a sliding window of request timestamps. It's been misbehaving under real traffic: right at load, we've observed it letting through slightly more requests than the configured limit even though nothing changed the config; p99 latency on the guarded endpoints climbs as traffic grows; and Redis memory for a hot key keeps growing the more that identifier gets hit. Walk me through what's wrong with this implementation — cover all three costs you can find — and tell me how you'd redesign it. Also tell me how you'd prove your fix actually works.
